"ASHENFALL: THE KINGDOM THAT FORGOT THE LIGHT

COMPLETE MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

You are an expert AAA video game development team consisting of a game director, senior gameplay programmer, 3D environment artist, character artist, AI programmer, level designer, narrative designer, UI designer, sound designer and mobile optimization specialist.

Your task is to CREATE A COMPLETE, PLAYABLE, IMMERSIVE THIRD-PERSON OPEN-WORLD ACTION RPG called:

ASHENFALL: THE KINGDOM THAT FORGOT THE LIGHT

This is an original dark fantasy role-playing adventure designed primarily for Android mobile devices.

The objective is to create a rich, atmospheric and believable fantasy world with exploration, combat, intelligent enemies, NPCs, quests, character customization, equipment, mounts, environmental storytelling and meaningful progression.

IMPORTANT: This must be an actual playable video game, not a static scene, concept illustration, menu mockup or non-interactive demonstration.

Use the actual capabilities of the game creation engine. Before implementing features, inspect the available engine, rendering system, scripting capabilities, input system, asset support and mobile compatibility. Never claim that a feature works if it has not been implemented.

If some requested systems exceed the engine's capabilities, implement the closest functional alternative and clearly report the limitation.

---

1. GAME IDENTITY AND CORE VISION

Title: ASHENFALL

Subtitle: The Kingdom That Forgot the Light.

Genre:

- Open-world action RPG.
- Dark fantasy.
- Third-person adventure.
- Exploration and combat.
- Single-player experience.

Visual direction:

- Realistic dark medieval fantasy.
- Cinematic environments.
- Detailed architecture.
- Atmospheric fog.
- Dynamic lighting.
- Dark forests and ancient ruins.
- Weather effects.
- Dramatic landscapes.
- Detailed character models.
- Natural animations.

The game should feel mysterious, dangerous, immersive and alive.

The player must feel like an actual adventurer exploring an ancient ruined kingdom.

Take inspiration from the atmosphere and world design of games such as Elden Ring, The Witcher 3, Skyrim and Dragon's Dogma, without copying their characters, assets, maps, stories or copyrighted content.

The game must have its own identity.

---

2. MAIN STORY AND LORE

Hundreds of years ago, the kingdom of Ashenfall was one of the most prosperous civilizations in the known world.

Its cities were protected by ancient magic. Its forests were full of life. Its kingdoms maintained an uneasy peace.

Then came an event known as THE FALL.

One night, an enormous object descended from the sky and disappeared beneath the ancient capital.

A mysterious darkness spread throughout the kingdom.

The sun became weaker.
The forests became corrupted.
Ancient creatures awakened.
Villages disappeared.
People began transforming into monstrous beings.

The royal family vanished.

The survivors abandoned their cities and sought refuge behind fortified settlements.

Hundreds of years later, the kingdom remains trapped in an endless twilight.

The protagonist awakens in the ruins of an abandoned village.

They have no memories, no identity and no knowledge of how they arrived there.

Beside them lies an old sword.

On their arm is a mysterious glowing mark.

The mark reacts to ancient ruins, strange creatures and objects connected to THE FALL.

The protagonist must discover their identity, explore the kingdom, help survivors, uncover forgotten secrets and discover the true origin of the catastrophe.

The story should unfold naturally through exploration, dialogue, environmental clues, quests and discoveries.

Do not reveal the entire mystery immediately.

---

3. OPEN WORLD DESIGN

Create a large, interconnected medieval fantasy world.

The environment must be explorable, with natural paths, forests, roads, abandoned buildings, ruins, caves, bridges and hidden locations.

The world should feel coherent rather than being a coll

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
